sentences.text: Vegavis iaai is an extinct bird belonging to the order Anseriformes and the family Vegaviidae, serving as the sole known member of its genus.
Its specific name, iaai, derives from the acronym for the Argentine Antarctic Institute, the organization leading scientific expeditions to the continent.
The fossil exhibits osteosclerosis, a condition involving thickened bone tissue also observed in the related species Polarornis.
The type specimen, cataloged as MLP 93-I-3-1, was discovered in 1992 within deposits at Cape Lamb on Vega Island, Antarctica.
This species was formally described only in 2005 because the fossil consists of extremely delicate remains of a bird trapped inside a concretion.
The Vegavis fossil specimen is currently housed in the Museo de La Plata in Argentina.
Researchers utilized computed axial tomography scans to produce clearer images of the bone structure without risking damage to the fragile bones.
The species was described by Irazoqui et al.
Vegavis belongs to the clade Anseriformes.
Among living birds, Vegavis is most closely related to the family Anatidae, which includes ducks and geese, though it is not viewed as a direct ancestor of that group.
Vegavis iaai lived during the Late Cretaceous, specifically the Maastrichtian stage of Antarctica, approximately 65 million years ago.
The genus Vegavis existed from 72.2 to 66 million years ago throughout the Maastrichtian stage.
The geological stratum containing Vegavis geitononesos is dated to the uppermost Maastrichtian.
Vegavis possessed a high metabolism that enabled it to survive in the high latitudes of Antarctica.
The palatine morphology of Vegavis displays a combination of primitive and unique characters within Neognathae, a point of discussion among researchers.
